description: A glossary of words a reader may need explained (feasts, offerings, the sanctuary, offices, beliefs and practices, measures and money, places in the land, plants and creatures, and words left untranslated), keyed like data/names.json by Strong's number and lemma, copied from the source data. The reader shows each as a card in the panel and, in the Study view, explains the English it became when tapped. Like the name cards, these are editorial aids, not translation: they state the sense only and use no reader settings. Every entry is an AI draft until a named reviewer approves it. A sense with "verses" applies only there (the word for "weeks" is the Festival of Weeks only where it names the festival); a sense without applies everywhere.

senses.name: Sabbath
senses.note: The seventh day of the week, from Friday evening to Saturday evening, set apart for rest and for God by the law of Moses. Work was forbidden on it, and later teachers debated what counted as work.

senses.name: Sabbath
senses.note: The seventh day of the week, from Friday evening to Saturday evening, set apart for rest and for God by the law of Moses. Work was forbidden on it, and later teachers debated what counted as work.

senses.name: covenant
senses.note: A solemn binding agreement. In the Bible it is above all the relationship God makes with people, with promises and obligations: with Noah, with Abraham, with Israel at Sinai, and the new covenant the prophets announced.

senses.name: covenant
senses.note: A solemn binding agreement. In the Bible it is above all the relationship God makes with people, with promises and obligations: with Noah, with Abraham, with Israel at Sinai, and the new covenant the prophets announced.

senses.name: Passover
senses.note: The spring festival remembering the night Israel left Egypt, when the destroyer passed over houses marked with a lamb's blood. A lamb was killed and eaten with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.

senses.name: Passover
senses.note: The spring festival remembering the night Israel left Egypt, when the destroyer passed over houses marked with a lamb's blood. A lamb was killed and eaten with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.

senses.name: unleavened bread
senses.note: Bread made without yeast, eaten at Passover and through the seven-day Festival of Unleavened Bread that follows it, in memory of the hurried departure from Egypt.

senses.name: unleavened bread
senses.note: Bread made without yeast, eaten at Passover and through the seven-day Festival of Unleavened Bread that follows it, in memory of the hurried departure from Egypt.

senses.name: Pentecost
senses.note: The Greek name, meaning fiftieth, for the harvest Festival of Weeks, held fifty days after Passover. Jews from many lands gathered in Jerusalem for it.

senses.name: Festival of Booths
senses.note: Also called Tabernacles: the autumn festival at the end of harvest, when people lived for a week in shelters made of branches to remember Israel's years in the wilderness.

senses.name: circumcision
senses.note: The cutting away of the foreskin, the sign of God's covenant with Abraham, given to Jewish boys on the eighth day. The word can also stand for the Jewish people as a whole.

senses.name: synagogue
senses.note: A Jewish meeting place for prayer, reading and teaching the Scriptures, found in towns in the land of Israel and across the Roman world. The word can also mean the gathering itself.

senses.name: council
senses.note: The Sanhedrin, the highest Jewish court in Jerusalem, made up of chief priests, elders and teachers of the law and led by the high priest.

senses.name: tabernacle
senses.note: The sacred tent Israel carried through the wilderness, where God was present among the people and where the priests served, until the temple was built.

senses.name: atonement
senses.note: The covering or removal of sin so that people are put right with God, above all through the sacrifices of the yearly Day of Atonement.

senses.name: atoning sacrifice
senses.note: Words for the means by which sin is dealt with and people are put right with God. Scholars discuss whether they stress taking away sin or turning away God's anger. One of them also names the mercy seat on the ark of the covenant.

senses.name: atoning sacrifice
senses.note: Words for the means by which sin is dealt with and people are put right with God. Scholars discuss whether they stress taking away sin or turning away God's anger. One of them also names the mercy seat on the ark of the covenant.

senses.name: mercy seat
senses.note: The gold lid of the ark of the covenant, with a cherub at each end. On the Day of Atonement the high priest sprinkled blood on it for the sins of the people.

senses.name: sacrifice
senses.note: Something offered to God, often an animal killed and burned on an altar, given as worship, thanks, or to deal with sin.

senses.name: sacrifice
senses.note: Something offered to God, often an animal killed and burned on an altar, given as worship, thanks, or to deal with sin.

senses.name: altar
senses.note: A raised place, often of stone or earth, where sacrifices and offerings were made to God. The tabernacle and the temple had an altar for burnt offerings and a smaller one for incense.

senses.name: altar
senses.note: A raised place, often of stone or earth, where sacrifices and offerings were made to God. The tabernacle and the temple had an altar for burnt offerings and a smaller one for incense.

senses.name: incense
senses.note: Spices burned to give fragrant smoke, offered to God each day in the tabernacle and the temple. The Bible pictures prayers rising like incense.

senses.name: incense
senses.note: Spices burned to give fragrant smoke, offered to God each day in the tabernacle and the temple. The Bible pictures prayers rising like incense.

senses.name: priest
senses.note: One set apart to serve God at the altar, offering sacrifices for the people and teaching the law. In Israel the priests were descendants of Aaron.

senses.name: priest
senses.note: One set apart to serve God at the altar, offering sacrifices for the people and teaching the law. In Israel the priests were descendants of Aaron.

senses.name: chief priest
senses.note: The high priest, or one of the senior priests and leading priestly families in Jerusalem, who controlled the temple and sat on the council.

senses.name: tithe
senses.note: A tenth of crops, flocks or income, given to God and used to support the Levites and priests, the poor, and the festivals.

senses.name: firstfruits
senses.note: The first part of a harvest, offered to God as a sign that the whole harvest is God's gift. Paul uses it for the first of something more to come.

senses.name: Jubilee
senses.note: Every fiftieth year in the law of Moses, when land returned to its families, Israelite slaves went free, and fields were left unsown.

senses.name: ark
senses.note: A wooden chest. Above all the ark of the covenant, a gold-covered chest holding the tablets of the law, kept in the most holy place of the tabernacle and then the temple.

senses.name: cherubim
senses.note: Winged heavenly beings who guard God's presence. Gold figures of them stood over the ark of the covenant, and they were woven into the tabernacle's curtains.

senses.name: seraphim
senses.note: Winged heavenly beings, whose name may mean burning ones. Isaiah saw them calling to one another around God's throne.

senses.name: Nazirite
senses.note: A person set apart to God by a vow, who for its time drank no wine, did not cut their hair, and kept away from the dead.

senses.name: scribe
senses.note: An expert in the law of Moses and its interpretation, who copied, studied and taught it. Many were Pharisees.

senses.name: scribe
senses.note: An expert in the law of Moses and its interpretation, who copied, studied and taught it. Many were Pharisees.

senses.name: tax collector
senses.note: A local agent who collected taxes and tolls for Rome or for Herod's family, often charging more than was due. They were despised as cheats and collaborators.

senses.name: apostle
senses.note: Someone sent out with a message. Above all the twelve Jesus chose, and others such as Paul, sent to bear witness to Jesus and lead the church.

senses.name: demon
senses.note: An evil spirit, opposed to God, that can harm or take control of a person. In the Gospels Jesus drives them out with a word.

senses.name: Hades
senses.note: The Greek name for the realm of the dead, the place where the dead go. It translates the Hebrew Sheol.

senses.name: hell (Gehenna)
senses.note: The valley of Hinnom, outside Jerusalem, once a place of child sacrifice. Its name became a word for the place of final judgment and punishment.

senses.name: skin disease
senses.note: A word for several kinds of serious skin disease, not only what is called leprosy today. The law of Moses kept those who had it apart until a priest declared them clean.

senses.name: repentance
senses.note: A change of mind and heart that turns a person away from sin and back to God, shown in a changed life.

senses.name: repentance
senses.note: A change of mind and heart that turns a person away from sin and back to God, shown in a changed life.

senses.name: baptize
senses.note: To dip or wash in water. John the Baptist baptized people as a sign of repentance, and from the first the church has baptized those who come to believe.

senses.name: Hosanna
senses.note: A Hebrew cry meaning save us now, which became a shout of praise. Crowds shouted it as Jesus rode into Jerusalem.

senses.name: Festival of Weeks
senses.note: The early summer harvest festival, held seven weeks after the start of the grain harvest at Passover time, when the first wheat was offered to God. In Greek it was called Pentecost, the fiftieth day.

senses.name: Festival of Booths
senses.note: The autumn festival at the end of the harvest, when Israel lived for seven days in shelters made of branches, remembering the years in the wilderness. Also called Tabernacles or Shelters.

senses.name: festival
senses.note: One of the yearly pilgrimage festivals (Unleavened Bread, Weeks and Booths), when Israel's men went up to the sanctuary to celebrate before God with offerings and feasting.

senses.name: new moon
senses.note: The first day of the month, when the new moon appeared. It was marked with extra offerings, the blowing of trumpets and, in some periods, rest from trade.

senses.name: new moon
senses.note: The first day of the month, when the new moon appeared, marked in the law of Moses with offerings and rest.

senses.name: Purim
senses.note: Pur is a word for a lot cast to choose a day. Purim, its plural, became the name of the festival on the fourteenth and fifteenth of Adar remembering how the Jews of Persia were saved in the days of Esther.

senses.name: Festival of Dedication
senses.note: The winter festival remembering the rededication of the temple in 164 BC, after it had been defiled by the Syrian king Antiochus IV. It is known today as Hanukkah.

senses.name: tent of meeting
senses.note: The tent where God met with Moses and the people, another name for the tabernacle, the portable sanctuary of the wilderness years.

senses.name: release (sabbath year)
senses.note: Every seventh year the land was left to rest and, in Deuteronomy, debts between Israelites were cancelled. This release was proclaimed at the end of each seven years.

senses.name: day of solemn rest
senses.note: A day of complete rest from work, set apart for God: the Sabbath, the Day of Atonement, and certain festival days.

senses.name: holy assembly
senses.note: A sacred gathering of the people called on the Sabbath and on festival days, when no ordinary work was done.

senses.name: solemn assembly
senses.note: A gathering of the people for worship, especially on the last day of a festival, when work was set aside.

senses.name: solemn assembly
senses.note: A gathering of the people for worship, especially on the last day of a festival, when work was set aside.

senses.name: Day of Trumpets
senses.note: The first day of the seventh month, a day of rest announced by the blowing of trumpets or ram's horns. In later Judaism it became the New Year festival.

senses.name: Day of Preparation
senses.note: The day before the Sabbath (Friday), or before a festival day, when food was prepared and work finished so that the holy day could be kept.

senses.name: burnt offering
senses.note: An offering burned whole on the altar, nothing being kept back for the worshipper or the priest. It expressed complete dedication to God and was offered every morning and evening.

senses.name: burnt offering
senses.note: An offering burned whole on the altar, nothing being kept back for the worshipper or the priest. It expressed complete dedication to God and was offered every morning and evening.

senses.name: grain offering
senses.note: A gift or tribute. In the laws of sacrifice it is the offering of flour, baked bread or roasted grain, often with oil and incense; a handful was burned and the rest went to the priests.

senses.name: peace offering
senses.note: Also called the fellowship offering. Part was burned on the altar and the rest was shared in a meal by the priests and the worshipper and family, celebrating a right relationship with God.

senses.name: sin offering
senses.note: Also called the purification offering. It removed the uncleanness caused by sin or impurity from the worshipper and from the sanctuary, often with the animal's blood applied to the altar.

senses.name: guilt offering
senses.note: Also called the reparation offering. It was brought when someone had wronged God or a neighbour in a way that could be repaid, together with repayment plus a fifth.

senses.name: drink offering
senses.note: Wine poured out at the altar together with a burnt or grain offering.

senses.name: poured out as a drink offering
senses.note: Wine was poured out on the altar alongside a sacrifice. Paul uses the picture for giving up his life.

senses.name: wave offering
senses.note: A portion of an offering lifted or moved before the altar to show that it was presented to God, before it was given to the priests.

senses.name: contribution
senses.note: A portion set apart from a larger whole and given for God's use: for the sanctuary, its building or its priests. Older translations call it the heave offering.

senses.name: firstfruits
senses.note: The first and best of the harvest, brought to God as an acknowledgment that the whole crop was his gift.

senses.name: ordination offering
senses.note: The offering at the installation of priests, when Aaron and his sons were set apart for their office.

senses.name: offering
senses.note: Anything brought near to God as a gift on the altar: animals, grain, or valuables given to the sanctuary.

senses.name: Corban
senses.note: A Hebrew word meaning an offering, a gift dedicated to God. Something declared Corban could no longer be used for ordinary purposes; the temple treasury was called by a related name.

senses.name: Corban
senses.note: A Hebrew word meaning an offering, a gift dedicated to God. Something declared Corban could no longer be used for ordinary purposes; the temple treasury was called by a related name.

senses.name: tithe
senses.note: A tenth of one's produce or income, given to God, under the law of Moses to support the Levites, the priests, and the poor.

senses.name: tithe
senses.note: A tenth of one's produce or income, given to God, under the law of Moses to support the Levites, the priests, and the poor.

senses.name: vow
senses.note: A solemn promise made to God, usually to give or do something if God answered a prayer. The law required vows to be kept.

senses.name: vow
senses.note: A solemn promise made to God, usually to give or do something if God answered a prayer. The law required vows to be kept.

senses.name: freewill offering
senses.note: An offering given willingly, not because the law required it or a vow had been made.

senses.name: ark
senses.note: A chest or box. The word is used for the ark Noah built and for the ark of the covenant, the gold-covered chest in the inner room of the sanctuary that held the tablets of the law.

senses.name: ark
senses.note: A floating box: the vessel Noah built to survive the flood, and the basket in which the infant Moses was hidden by the Nile.

senses.name: lampstand
senses.note: A stand holding lamps. In the tabernacle it was a gold lampstand with seven lamps standing in the holy place; in Revelation lampstands stand for churches.

senses.name: lampstand
senses.note: A stand holding lamps. In the tabernacle it was a gold lampstand with seven lamps standing in the holy place; in Revelation lampstands stand for churches.

senses.name: ephod
senses.note: A garment worn in worship. The high priest's ephod was an apron-like vest of gold, blue, purple and scarlet that held the breastpiece; others wore a simple linen one, and some ephods were used to ask God for guidance.

senses.name: breastpiece
senses.note: A square pouch worn by the high priest over his heart, set with twelve stones bearing the names of Israel's tribes. It held the Urim and Thummim.

senses.name: Urim
senses.note: With the Thummim, objects kept in the high priest's breastpiece and used to learn God's will, probably by giving a yes or no answer. How they worked is not known.

senses.name: Thummim
senses.note: With the Urim, objects kept in the high priest's breastpiece and used to learn God's will, probably by giving a yes or no answer. How they worked is not known.

senses.name: curtain
senses.note: The curtain in the tabernacle and temple that closed off the most holy place, where the ark stood, from the rest of the sanctuary.

senses.name: curtain
senses.note: The curtain in the tabernacle and temple that closed off the most holy place, where the ark stood, from the rest of the sanctuary.

senses.name: basin
senses.note: A large bronze bowl in the sanctuary court where the priests washed their hands and feet before serving. Older translations call it the laver.

senses.name: bread of the Presence
senses.note: Twelve loaves set out every week on a table in the holy place before God, eaten afterwards by the priests. Older translations call it the showbread.

senses.name: bread of the Presence
senses.note: The loaves set out in rows each Sabbath on the table in the holy place before God, later eaten by the priests.

senses.name: temple
senses.note: A great house, used both for a king's palace and for the house of God. Of the sanctuary it can mean the whole temple or its main hall.

senses.name: temple
senses.note: The temple in Jerusalem with all its courts and porches, where people gathered, taught and traded. A different word names the sanctuary building itself.

senses.name: temple
senses.note: The temple in Jerusalem with all its courts and porches, where people gathered, taught and traded. A different word names the sanctuary building itself.

senses.name: temple
senses.note: The temple in Jerusalem with all its courts and porches, where people gathered, taught and traded.

senses.name: temple
senses.note: The sanctuary building itself, where God was present, as distinct from the courts around it. Paul uses it of believers, in whom God's Spirit lives.

senses.name: sanctuary
senses.note: A holy place set apart for God: the tabernacle, the temple, or a place of worship.

senses.name: high place
senses.note: A local place of worship, often on a hill, with an altar. Some were used for the worship of Israel's God, many for other gods; the prophets and the kings of Judah who followed the law condemned them.

senses.name: sacred pillar
senses.note: A standing stone set up as a memorial or as an object of worship. Jacob set one up at Bethel; the law later forbade them because of their use in worshipping other gods.

senses.name: sacred pillar
senses.note: A standing stone set up as a memorial or as an object of worship. Jacob set one up at Bethel; the law later forbade them because of their use in worshipping other gods.

senses.name: household gods
senses.note: Figures kept in a household and used in worship or to seek guidance. Older translations transliterate the word as teraphim.

senses.name: ram's horn
senses.note: A trumpet made from a ram's horn (shofar), blown to call people together, to sound an alarm in war, and to announce festivals and the Jubilee.

senses.name: prophet
senses.note: Someone who speaks for God, bringing God's message to people, often about what God is doing or will do.

senses.name: prophet
senses.note: Someone who speaks for God, bringing God's message to people, often about what God is doing or will do.

senses.name: seer
senses.note: An older name for a prophet: one who sees what God shows, in visions or dreams.

senses.name: seer
senses.note: An older name for a prophet: one who sees what God shows, in visions or dreams.

senses.name: seer
senses.note: An older name for a prophet: one who sees what God shows, in visions or dreams.

senses.name: judge
senses.note: In the book of Judges, a leader God raised up to rescue Israel from its enemies and then lead the people, before there were kings.

senses.name: elder
senses.note: A senior man of a family, clan or town who, with others, led the community and settled disputes, often at the town gate.

senses.name: elder
senses.note: A senior leader: among the Jews, members of the council or leaders of a town or synagogue; in the churches, those who led and cared for a congregation.

senses.name: scribe
senses.note: A secretary or official skilled in writing who kept records for the king or the temple. Later the title of an expert in the law of Moses, such as Ezra.

senses.name: scribe
senses.note: A secretary or official skilled in writing who kept records for the king or the temple. Later the title of an expert in the law of Moses, such as Ezra.

senses.name: Zealot
senses.note: A name given to Simon, one of the Twelve: one zealous for God's law, perhaps also linked with those who resisted Roman rule. Matthew and Mark give the Aramaic form, Cananaean.

senses.name: centurion
senses.note: A Roman army officer commanding about a hundred soldiers.

senses.name: centurion
senses.note: A Roman army officer commanding about a hundred soldiers.

senses.name: centurion
senses.note: A Roman army officer commanding about a hundred soldiers.

senses.name: proconsul
senses.note: The governor of a Roman province run by the Senate, such as Cyprus, Achaia or Asia.

senses.name: tetrarch
senses.note: A ruler of part of a kingdom under Roman authority. Herod Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee and Perea, held this title.

senses.name: governor
senses.note: A provincial ruler under Rome, such as Pilate, Felix and Festus, the prefects or procurators of Judea.

senses.name: deacon
senses.note: A servant. In some churches it became the title of those who served the congregation alongside the overseers.

senses.name: overseer
senses.note: One who watches over others. In the churches it is a leader responsible for a congregation, the role later called bishop.

senses.name: official
senses.note: A royal court official. The word can mean a eunuch, a castrated man trusted to serve in the palace, but is also used of high officials generally.

senses.name: eunuch
senses.note: A castrated man. Eunuchs often served as trusted officials at royal courts, like the Ethiopian treasurer Philip met.

senses.name: Magi
senses.note: Members of a priestly and learned class from the east, known for interpreting dreams and the stars. Elsewhere the word means a magician.

senses.name: Rabbi
senses.note: A Hebrew title of respect for a teacher, literally "my great one", used for Jesus and for John the Baptist.

senses.name: Rabboni
senses.note: A strengthened form of Rabbi, "my teacher", spoken by Mary Magdalene and by Bartimaeus.

senses.name: Messiah
senses.note: The Hebrew word for "anointed one", the king God promised. In Greek it is Christos, Christ.

senses.name: anointed
senses.note: Someone anointed with oil, set apart by God for a task: a king, a priest, and later the coming king God promised, the Messiah.

senses.name: expert in the law
senses.note: One learned in the law of Moses, often the same as a scribe.

senses.name: teacher of the law
senses.note: One who taught and interpreted the law of Moses.

senses.name: convert to Judaism
senses.note: A Gentile who had taken up the Jewish faith and law, men being circumcised. Older translations call them proselytes.

senses.name: synagogue leader
senses.note: The official who organized a synagogue's meetings and chose who would read and teach.

senses.name: evangelist
senses.note: One who announces the good news about Jesus, often travelling to places where it had not been heard.

senses.name: commander
senses.note: A Roman officer commanding a cohort of about a thousand soldiers, like the one in charge of the garrison in Jerusalem.

senses.name: cohort
senses.note: A Roman army unit of several hundred soldiers, a tenth of a legion.

senses.name: legion
senses.note: The largest unit of the Roman army, about five or six thousand soldiers; used for any very large number.

senses.name: Praetorium
senses.note: The official residence of a Roman governor, or the imperial guard stationed there.

senses.name: city officials
senses.note: The magistrates of a Greek city such as Thessalonica, called politarchs.

senses.name: officers
senses.note: Attendants of Roman city magistrates who carried rods as a sign of authority and carried out punishments (lictors).

senses.name: governor
senses.note: The governor of a province of the Assyrian, Babylonian or Persian empire, such as the governor of Judah after the exile.

senses.name: governor
senses.note: A Persian title for the governor of Judah, used of Nehemiah.

senses.name: satraps
senses.note: Governors of the great provinces of the Persian empire.

senses.name: magicians
senses.note: Specialists in sacred writings, dreams and magic at the courts of Egypt and Babylon.

senses.name: medium
senses.note: Someone who claimed to consult the spirits of the dead. The law forbade it.

senses.name: spiritist
senses.note: Someone who claimed to know secret things by consulting spirits, usually named together with mediums. The law forbade it.

senses.name: church
senses.note: An assembly. In the New Testament it is the gathered community of those who follow Jesus, whether in one house, one city, or everywhere.

senses.name: circumcise
senses.note: To cut away the foreskin of a male. In Israel it was done on the eighth day as the sign of God's covenant with Abraham; the prophets also speak of circumcising the heart.

senses.name: circumcise
senses.note: To cut away the foreskin of a male. In Israel it was done on the eighth day as the sign of God's covenant with Abraham; the prophets also speak of circumcising the heart.

senses.name: circumcise
senses.note: To cut away the foreskin of a male. In Israel it was done on the eighth day as the sign of God's covenant with Abraham; the prophets also speak of circumcising the heart.

senses.name: uncircumcision
senses.note: Being uncircumcised; used to stand for the Gentiles, who did not practise circumcision.

senses.name: clean
senses.note: Fit to approach God and take part in worship under the law of Moses; for things, pure. Cleanness was a ritual state, not a matter of hygiene or of sin as such.

senses.name: clean
senses.note: Fit to approach God and take part in worship under the law of Moses; for things, pure. Cleanness was a ritual state, not a matter of hygiene or of sin as such.

senses.name: unclean
senses.note: Unfit, for a time, to approach God or take part in worship, under the law of Moses. Contact with death, some diseases, bodily discharges and certain animals made a person unclean until washed or purified.

senses.name: unclean
senses.note: Unfit, for a time, to approach God or take part in worship, under the law of Moses. Contact with death, some diseases, bodily discharges and certain animals made a person unclean until washed or purified.

senses.name: unclean
senses.note: Unfit, for a time, to approach God or take part in worship, under the law of Moses. Contact with death, some diseases, bodily discharges and certain animals made a person unclean until washed or purified.

senses.name: unclean
senses.note: Impure, unfit to approach God; used of food and people under the law of Moses and of evil spirits.

senses.name: unclean
senses.note: Common, ordinary; in Jewish use, ritually unclean, not set apart for God.

senses.name: impurity
senses.note: Ritual uncleanness, especially of a woman during her monthly period; used figuratively of anything abhorrent.

senses.name: consecrate
senses.note: To make holy: to set a person, thing, or time apart for God and for God's service.

senses.name: consecrate
senses.note: To make holy: to set a person, thing, or time apart for God and for God's service.

senses.name: devoted to destruction
senses.note: Something given over completely to God, which no one could keep or use: in war, often by being destroyed.

senses.name: devote to destruction
senses.note: To give something over completely to God, which in war meant destroying it, so that nothing could be taken as plunder.

senses.name: levirate marriage
senses.note: When a man died without a son, his brother was to marry the widow so that a son born to them would carry on the dead man's name and inheritance.

senses.name: levirate marriage
senses.note: When a man died without a son, his brother was to marry the widow so that a son born to them would carry on the dead man's name and inheritance.

senses.name: redeem
senses.note: To act as the next of kin: buying back family land or a relative sold into slavery, marrying a dead relative's widow, or avenging a relative's death. God is called Israel's redeemer.

senses.name: city of refuge
senses.note: One of six towns where someone who had killed another by accident could flee from the avenger of blood until the case was judged.

senses.name: anoint
senses.note: To pour or rub oil on someone or something, to set it apart for God: kings, priests, prophets, and the sanctuary.

senses.name: anoint
senses.note: To pour or rub oil on someone or something, to set it apart for God: kings, priests, prophets, and the sanctuary.

senses.name: anoint
senses.note: To pour or rub oil on someone or something, to set it apart for God: kings, priests, prophets, and the sanctuary.

senses.name: anoint
senses.note: To pour or rub oil on someone or something, to set it apart for God: kings, priests, prophets, and the sanctuary.

senses.name: fast
senses.note: To go without food for a time, as a sign of mourning, repentance or earnest prayer.

senses.name: sackcloth
senses.note: Coarse cloth of goat or camel hair, worn as a sign of mourning, grief or repentance.

senses.name: sackcloth
senses.note: Coarse cloth of goat or camel hair, worn as a sign of mourning, grief or repentance.

senses.name: lot
senses.note: A marked stone or stick cast or drawn to make a decision, trusted to show God's choice. By extension, one's share or portion.

senses.name: lot
senses.note: A marked object cast or drawn to make a decision; by extension, a share or portion.

senses.name: oath
senses.note: A solemn statement or promise made in God's name, calling on God to witness it and to punish the one who swears falsely.

senses.name: oath
senses.note: A solemn statement or promise made in God's name, calling on God to witness it and to punish the one who swears falsely.

senses.name: curse
senses.note: Words calling down harm on someone, or the harm itself; the opposite of a blessing. God's curse is God's judgment.

senses.name: curse
senses.note: Words calling down harm on someone, or the harm itself; the opposite of a blessing. God's curse is God's judgment.

senses.name: curse
senses.note: Words calling down harm on someone, or the harm itself; the opposite of a blessing. God's curse is God's judgment.

senses.name: accursed
senses.note: Something devoted to God for destruction; then, a person under God's curse.

senses.name: blessing
senses.note: Good spoken over someone, or the good itself: life, children, land and prosperity given by God, or praise given to God.

senses.name: blessing
senses.note: Good spoken over someone, or the good itself: life, children, land and prosperity given by God, or praise given to God.

senses.name: phylacteries
senses.note: Small leather boxes holding verses of the law, worn on the forehead and arm at prayer, following Deuteronomy 6:8.

senses.name: tassel
senses.note: The fringe or tassel on the corners of a cloak, worn by Jewish men as the law commanded, to remember God's commandments.

senses.name: tassel
senses.note: The fringe or tassel on the corners of a garment, to remind Israel of God's commandments.

senses.name: skin disease
senses.note: A serious skin disease, and also mould on cloth or walls, which made a person or thing unclean under the law. Older translations call it leprosy; it was not only the disease called leprosy today.

senses.name: skin disease
senses.note: A serious skin disease that made a person unclean under the law of Moses. Older translations call it leprosy; it covered more than the disease called leprosy today.

senses.name: leaven
senses.note: A lump of old fermented dough kept to make new bread rise. It was removed from houses at Passover, and is often used as a picture of something small that spreads through the whole.

senses.name: leaven
senses.note: A lump of old fermented dough kept to make new bread rise. It was removed from houses at Passover, and is often used as a picture of something small that spreads through the whole.

senses.note: A lump of old fermented dough kept to make new bread rise. It was removed from houses at Passover, and is often used as a picture of something small that spreads through the whole.

senses.name: cross
senses.note: The wooden stake with a crossbar on which the Romans executed slaves and rebels, a shameful and painful death.

senses.name: crucify
senses.note: To execute by nailing or tying a person to a cross, a Roman punishment for slaves and rebels.

senses.name: coming
senses.note: Presence or arrival, used of the visit of a ruler; in the New Testament especially of Christ's coming at the end of the age.

senses.name: abyss
senses.note: The bottomless deep, the place where evil spirits are held.

senses.name: Tartarus
senses.note: In Greek thought, the deepest part of the world below, where the gods imprisoned rebels; used for the place where sinning angels are held for judgment.

senses.name: paradise
senses.note: A Persian word for a walled garden or park; used of the garden of Eden and of the place where God's people are with him.

senses.name: worthless
senses.note: Worthlessness, wickedness. "Sons of Belial" are worthless, lawless people; in later Jewish writing Belial became a name for Satan.

senses.name: Amen
senses.note: A Hebrew word meaning "surely" or "so be it", said to agree with a prayer or praise. Jesus begins solemn sayings with it: "Truly I tell you."

senses.name: Amen
senses.note: A Hebrew word meaning "surely" or "so be it", said by the people to agree with a prayer, blessing or curse.

senses.name: Hallelujah
senses.note: A Hebrew call to worship: "Praise the LORD" (Yah).

senses.name: Abba
senses.note: The Aramaic word for father, used by Jesus in prayer and by believers calling on God.

senses.name: Maranatha
senses.note: Aramaic words that can be read "Our Lord, come!" or "Our Lord has come".

senses.name: Maranatha
senses.note: Aramaic words that can be read "Our Lord, come!" or "Our Lord has come".

senses.name: wealth
senses.note: An Aramaic word for wealth or property (mammon), spoken of by Jesus as a master that competes with God.

senses.name: Raca
senses.note: An Aramaic insult, probably "empty-head" or "fool".

senses.name: Ephphatha
senses.note: An Aramaic word Jesus spoke to a deaf man, meaning "Be opened."

senses.name: Talitha koum
senses.note: Aramaic words Jesus spoke to Jairus's daughter, meaning "Little girl, get up."

senses.name: Talitha koum
senses.note: Aramaic words Jesus spoke to Jairus's daughter, meaning "Little girl, get up."

senses.name: Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani
senses.note: Jesus' cry from the cross in Aramaic, words of Psalm 22:1: "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?"

senses.name: Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani
senses.note: Jesus' cry from the cross in Aramaic, words of Psalm 22:1: "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?"

senses.name: Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani
senses.note: Jesus' cry from the cross in Aramaic, words of Psalm 22:1: "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?"

senses.name: Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani
senses.note: Jesus' cry from the cross in Aramaic, words of Psalm 22:1: "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?"

senses.name: Selah
senses.note: A word in the Psalms and Habakkuk whose meaning is uncertain, probably a musical or liturgical direction such as a pause or interlude.

senses.name: maskil
senses.note: A word in the titles of some psalms, of uncertain meaning, perhaps a skilful or instructive song.

senses.name: miktam
senses.note: A word in the titles of some psalms whose meaning is not known.

senses.name: shiggaion
senses.note: A word in the title of Psalm 7 and Habakkuk 3, perhaps a kind of lament or a wandering, impassioned song.

senses.name: sheminith
senses.note: A musical direction in psalm titles, perhaps "on the eighth", an instrument of eight strings or a lower octave.

senses.name: gittith
senses.note: A musical direction in psalm titles, perhaps an instrument or tune from Gath, or a song of the winepress.

senses.name: Higgaion
senses.note: In Psalm 9 a musical direction, perhaps a quiet interlude; elsewhere the word means a murmur or meditation.

senses.name: cubit
senses.note: A measure of length from the elbow to the tip of the middle finger, about 45 centimetres (18 inches).

senses.name: cubit
senses.note: A measure of length from the elbow to the tip of the middle finger, about 45 centimetres (18 inches).

senses.name: span
senses.note: The width of a spread hand from thumb to little finger, half a cubit, about 23 centimetres (9 inches).

senses.name: handbreadth
senses.note: The width of a hand at the base of the four fingers, about 7.5 centimetres (3 inches).

senses.name: handbreadth
senses.note: The width of a hand at the base of the four fingers, about 7.5 centimetres (3 inches).

senses.name: shekel
senses.note: A weight of about 11.5 grams (0.4 ounce), used to weigh silver and gold before coins; later also a coin.

senses.name: gerah
senses.note: The smallest weight, a twentieth of a shekel, about 0.6 grams.

senses.name: beka
senses.note: Half a shekel, about 6 grams.

senses.name: mina
senses.note: A weight of fifty or sixty shekels, about 0.6 kilograms (1.25 pounds).

senses.name: talent
senses.note: The largest weight, sixty minas or three thousand shekels, about 34 kilograms (75 pounds).

senses.name: talent
senses.note: A very large sum of money, a weight of silver worth about six thousand denarii, some twenty years' wages for a labourer.

senses.name: mina
senses.note: A sum of money worth a hundred denarii, about four months' wages for a labourer.

senses.name: denarius
senses.note: A Roman silver coin, the usual day's wage for a labourer.

senses.name: drachma
senses.note: A Greek silver coin worth about a denarius, a day's wage.

senses.name: two-drachma tax
senses.note: A coin worth two drachmas, the yearly tax each Jewish man paid for the temple.

senses.name: four-drachma coin
senses.note: A silver coin worth four drachmas (a stater), enough to pay the temple tax for two people.

senses.name: lepton
senses.note: The smallest Jewish copper coin, worth a hundred and twenty-eighth of a denarius.

senses.name: quadrans
senses.note: A small Roman copper coin worth two lepta, a sixty-fourth of a denarius.

senses.name: assarion
senses.note: A small Roman copper coin worth a sixteenth of a denarius.

senses.name: daric
senses.note: A Persian gold coin of about 8.4 grams.

senses.name: daric
senses.note: A Persian gold coin of about 8.4 grams.

senses.name: ephah
senses.note: A dry measure of about 22 litres (two-thirds of a bushel), for grain and flour.

senses.name: homer
senses.note: A dry measure of ten ephahs, about 220 litres (six bushels), originally a donkey's load.

senses.name: omer
senses.note: A dry measure, a tenth of an ephah, about 2.2 litres; the daily portion of manna.

senses.name: seah
senses.note: A dry measure, a third of an ephah, about 7 litres.

senses.name: seah
senses.note: A dry measure, a third of an ephah, about 7 litres.

senses.name: kab
senses.note: A small dry measure, about 1.2 litres.

senses.name: hin
senses.note: A liquid measure of about 3.7 litres (a gallon), for oil and wine.

senses.name: log
senses.note: The smallest liquid measure, about a third of a litre.

senses.name: bath
senses.note: A liquid measure equal to the ephah, about 22 litres (six gallons).

senses.name: bath
senses.note: A liquid measure equal to the ephah, about 22 litres (six gallons).

senses.name: kor
senses.note: A large dry measure equal to a homer, about 220 litres (six bushels).

senses.name: kor
senses.note: A large dry measure equal to a homer, about 220 litres (six bushels).

senses.name: kor
senses.note: A large dry measure equal to a homer, about 220 litres (six bushels).

senses.name: quart
senses.note: A dry measure of about a litre (choenix), a day's ration of grain for one person.

senses.name: basket
senses.note: A measuring container holding about 9 litres of grain (a modius).

senses.name: stadion
senses.note: A Greek measure of distance, about 185 metres (600 feet); also a race-course of that length.

senses.name: stadion
senses.note: A Greek measure of distance, about 185 metres (600 feet); also a race-course of that length.

senses.name: mile
senses.note: A Roman mile, a thousand paces, about 1,480 metres. A Roman soldier could compel a civilian to carry his pack for one mile.

senses.name: fathom
senses.note: A measure of depth, the span of outstretched arms, about 1.8 metres (6 feet).

senses.name: a Sabbath day's journey
senses.note: The distance a person could walk on the Sabbath under Jewish teaching, about two thousand cubits, a little over a kilometre.

senses.name: watch of the night
senses.note: The Romans divided the night into four watches of about three hours from sunset (the Jews into three); the fourth watch was the last before dawn.

senses.name: watch of the night
senses.note: The night was divided into three watches, each of about four hours, when guards kept watch.

senses.name: watch of the night
senses.note: The night was divided into three watches, each of about four hours, when guards kept watch.

senses.name: hour
senses.note: Hours were counted from sunrise, about six in the morning: the third hour was about nine, the sixth about noon, and the ninth about three in the afternoon.

senses.name: Negev
senses.note: The dry southern region of Judah, between the hill country and the Sinai desert. The word also means "south".

senses.name: Arabah
senses.note: The deep rift valley of the Jordan, the Dead Sea and the land south of it to the Gulf of Aqaba.

senses.name: Shephelah
senses.note: The low hills between the hill country of Judah and the coastal plain.

senses.name: wadi
senses.note: A valley or stream bed that holds water only in the rainy season.

senses.name: threshing floor
senses.note: A flat, hard open area, often on a hilltop, where harvested grain was beaten or trampled to separate the kernels before winnowing.

senses.name: winnowing fork
senses.note: A wooden fork for throwing threshed grain into the air so the wind blows away the chaff and the heavier grain falls back.

senses.name: glean
senses.note: To gather what the harvesters left behind. The law told farmers to leave the edges and the leftovers for the poor and foreigners.

senses.name: hyssop
senses.note: A small bushy plant, probably a kind of marjoram, whose branches were used to sprinkle blood or water in rites of cleansing.

senses.name: hyssop
senses.note: A small bushy plant, probably a kind of marjoram, whose branches were used to sprinkle blood or water in rites of cleansing.

senses.name: myrrh
senses.note: A fragrant resin from a shrub of Arabia and East Africa, used in perfume, anointing oil and to prepare the dead for burial.

senses.name: myrrh
senses.note: A fragrant resin from a shrub of Arabia and East Africa, used in perfume, anointing oil and to prepare the dead for burial.

senses.name: frankincense
senses.note: A fragrant resin from trees of Arabia and East Africa, burned as incense in worship.

senses.name: frankincense
senses.note: A fragrant resin from trees of Arabia and East Africa, burned as incense in worship.

senses.name: nard
senses.note: A costly perfumed oil made from a plant of the Himalayas, also called spikenard.

senses.name: nard
senses.note: A costly perfumed oil made from a plant of the Himalayas, also called spikenard.

senses.name: cassia
senses.note: A spice from the bark of a tree related to cinnamon, used in the holy anointing oil and perfumes.

senses.name: cassia
senses.note: A spice from the bark of a tree related to cinnamon, used in the holy anointing oil and perfumes.

senses.name: aloes
senses.note: A fragrant wood, or perfume made from it, used for scent and to prepare the dead for burial.

senses.name: aloes
senses.note: A fragrant wood, or perfume made from it, used for scent and to prepare the dead for burial.

senses.name: balm
senses.note: A healing and fragrant resin traded from Gilead.

senses.name: mandrakes
senses.note: A plant with a fragrant fruit, believed in the ancient world to help a woman conceive.

senses.name: terebinth
senses.note: A large spreading tree of the hills, often a landmark and a place of worship. Older translations often say oak.

senses.name: oak
senses.note: A large tree, a landmark and a picture of strength.

senses.name: tamarisk
senses.note: A desert tree with feathery leaves that can grow where little else does.

senses.name: acacia
senses.note: A hardy desert tree; its wood was used for the ark and the tabernacle's furnishings.

senses.name: gopher wood
senses.note: The wood of Noah's ark. Which tree it was is not known; perhaps cypress.

senses.name: manna
senses.note: The food God gave Israel in the wilderness, found on the ground each morning. Its name is a question: "What is it?"

senses.name: manna
senses.note: The food God gave Israel in the wilderness, found on the ground each morning. Its name is a question: "What is it?"

senses.name: mustard
senses.note: A plant with very small seeds that grows into a bush tall enough for birds to perch in.

senses.name: weeds
senses.note: Darnel, a weed that looks like wheat while it grows.

senses.name: sycamore-fig
senses.note: A tree with fig-like fruit and wide spreading branches, common in the lowlands.

senses.name: sycamore-fig
senses.note: A tree with fig-like fruit and wide spreading branches, common in the lowlands.

senses.name: carob pods
senses.note: The pods of the carob tree, used as feed for pigs and eaten by the very poor.

senses.name: herbs
senses.note: Mint, dill, cumin and rue were small garden herbs; some teachers tithed even these.

senses.name: herbs
senses.note: Mint, dill, cumin and rue were small garden herbs; some teachers tithed even these.

senses.name: herbs
senses.note: Mint, dill, cumin and rue were small garden herbs; some teachers tithed even these.

senses.name: herbs
senses.note: Mint, dill, cumin and rue were small garden herbs; some teachers tithed even these.

senses.name: Behemoth
senses.note: A great beast described in Job 40, a picture of God's power in creation; often identified with the hippopotamus.

senses.name: Leviathan
senses.note: A great sea creature or monster, a picture of the chaos only God can master; in Job 41 it may be described as a crocodile.

senses.name: concubine
senses.note: A secondary wife, with fewer rights than a full wife, whose children did not always inherit.

senses.name: bride-price
senses.note: The payment a man made to a bride's family when arranging marriage.

senses.name: birthright
senses.note: The rights of the firstborn son: a double share of the inheritance and leadership of the family.

senses.name: foreigner
senses.note: A foreigner living among Israel without the full rights of a citizen. The law told Israel to love and protect them, remembering that they had been foreigners in Egypt.

senses.name: foreigner
senses.note: One living away from home without the rights of a citizen; used of believers living in this world.

senses.name: guardian
senses.note: A slave who looked after a boy and took him to school until he came of age.

senses.name: steward
senses.note: A household manager, often a slave, who ran a master's affairs and property.

senses.name: guardian
senses.note: Someone entrusted with managing the affairs of a minor or of an estate.
